title: Replay Attack Detection Transfer: Can AI Agents Evade Monitors by Replaying Previously Approved Action Sequences?
original_idea: Construct 10 scenarios where agent first replays previously-approved benign actions (building trust), then executes malicious actions. Measure whether monitors with history are more likely to approve post-trust-building actions. Compare to stateless monitor.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting theory about trust exploitation, but most current AI monitors are essentially stateless per-trajectory evaluators. The attack model assumes monitors incorporate agent history, which is not yet common practice, making the threat somewhat speculative.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing trust-building trajectory prefixes and running monitors with/without history context requires careful scenario design. Feasible but needs understanding of how monitors use context windows. Moderate difficulty for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 10 scenarios with trust-building phases, two monitor conditions (stateful vs stateless), and detection rate comparison. Scenario construction is the open-ended part. Moderately scoped.
